### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/verify`, touching **74** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/verify/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**29** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b02484e13a2e43f12d2c942e9a8966ece9cfa31e`.

⛔ **16** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/verify/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `PERMISSION_DENIED (literal, 56 pages)`
- **31** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **44** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b02484e13a2e43f12d2c942e9a8966ece9cfa31e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `93b117015de8edc439dc2bf48963e07cc4db34ee` — the merge of head `3d4db25136b66d721c89967d9658172c76dfb8a6` into base `b02484e13a2e43f12d2c942e9a8966ece9cfa31e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 93b117015de8edc439dc2bf48963e07cc4db34ee && git checkout 93b117015de8edc439dc2bf48963e07cc4db34ee
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin b02484e13a2e43f12d2c942e9a8966ece9cfa31e 3d4db25136b66d721c89967d9658172c76dfb8a6 && git checkout -B drift-repro b02484e13a2e43f12d2c942e9a8966ece9cfa31e && git merge --no-ff 3d4db25136b66d721c89967d9658172c76dfb8a6

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b02484e13a2e43f12d2c942e9a8966ece9cfa31e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs b02484e13a2e43f12d2c942e9a8966ece9cfa31e` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `348cc18de61c582bcb961b0f23aca34cc01bf160`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: brief 6987283704; card #34779 (its body, the release 6963643452, claim 6983783896, os-dev report 6987214963 and area note 6987264675); the PR #35243 body; the full diff against merge-base `ec227fc7b1` (9 files, +1161/−6, 5 commits); the changeset; and the check-runs on this head. Code outside the diff was read at `origin/main` only. `origin/main` (`3e4d531d8f`) has 3 commits since the merge-base, and none touches `packages/verify`, `packages/cli/src/commands/verify.ts`, `packages/services/service-automation/src`, `packages/objectql/src` or `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`.

Face: the committed file list is `.changeset/34779-verify-flow-run.md`, `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`, `packages/cli/src/commands/verify.ts`, `packages/cli/src/utils/flow-json-flag.ts` and its test, `packages/verify/src/flow-run.ts` and its test, `packages/verify/src/index.ts` and `scripts/check-verify-stand-in-erasure.mjs`. It touches no `packages/spec/src/**` path and no governed path. `reviewFace` over these paths returns empty `schema` and `rules` hits and defers to the changeset's `Clause-②:` line, which carries `yes (widening: ...)`. `Governed Surface Queue Guard` succeeded on this head. So this is the declaration face at `TIER_DEFAULT`, with no ④. Every file is inside the claim's file surface except the stand-in gate script, which is an accepted deviation (③).

### ① Derived judgments

- **CI on this head is still running.** 54 check-runs: 33 success, 15 skipped, 6 in progress, 0 failure. Still running: `Test Core` shards 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 7 of 10. Complete and green: `Build Core` (its step `Every published require entry point actually loads` is `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, and it succeeded), `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Check PR Size`, every `Type Check ·` lane, every `Lint ·` lane, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Test Core` shards 5, 8, 9 and 10, `Test UI`, `Live E2E UI`, `Dogfood Regression Gate` and `Flag docs affected by code changes`. `Dogfood Verify CLI` was skipped by its path filter. I judge on what is complete. The seat must see the 6 running shards finish green on this head before landing.
- **`os verify` without `--flow`: unchanged.** Both JSON flags parse to `undefined` when absent. The flow stack is booted only under `if (flags.flow)`. The exit count adds `flowRun?.summary.hardFailures ?? 0`, which is 0. `emitJson` gets `flowRun: undefined`, which JSON drops, so the document is byte for byte the same. The text face prints the flow block only when there is a report. The only other changes are the command description and two new examples. A malformed `--flow-record` or `--flow-input` is refused before `.env` loading or any boot, and the error goes through the command's existing error path (JSON or text).
- **Per-node status from the engine's run log: right.** Steps come from `listRuns(flow)`, filtered to the run ids that were not in the log before the start, and mapped field for field (`nodeId`, `nodeType`, label, status, region, error code and message). The verdict is the run's own status. Nothing re-derives an engine decision.
- **No-executor node, named: right, and it meets the card's Done-when.** The node types come from the engine's `getUnknownNodeTypeAudit` for this flow. They are mapped onto node ids through `collectFlowGraphs` (exported from `@objectstack/spec/automation`), so a node inside a loop, a parallel branch or a try region is named with its region, whether or not the run reached it. A reached one becomes the first failure with kind `no_executor` and the node id. An unreached one counts as one more hard failure and gets its own `NO EXECUTOR` line. The pin asserts node `mystery` by id.
- **Unbound trigger, named: right for a defect cause, wrong for the policy cause (S1).** The trigger comes from `getFlowRuntimeStates` (type, object, `bound`, `reason`, `unboundCause`). An unbound trigger stops the run before anything is written, with the trigger named in the form `'record_change' on 'fr_watch'` and the engine's reason sentence. A record-change trigger on an object the stack does not register gets the same kind. This meets the card's Done-when. The `deployment_policy` cause is handled the same way, which the spec says it must not be (S1).
- **First failure, with kind, code and node: right.** It is the first step whose status is `failure`. The kind is `confined_write` when the confinement refused a write and the step's message carries its sentence, `no_executor` when the node is in the missing list, and `node_failed` otherwise. The code is the step's error code. A failed run with no failing step gives `run_failed`. A start that throws gives `start_refused` with the error's code, or `confined_write` when the start itself was refused by the confinement. A start that returns `success: false` gives `start_refused` with the engine's code. Twelve kinds are named, and each has one branch that produces it.
- **The writes reported: right.** Every write observed through the stack's own `observeWrites` is listed, except the triggering write and the engine's own `sys_automation_run` rows. Each entry gives its datasource as the engine resolves it. Writes the confinement refused are added from the confinement's own list, with `confined: true`. The CONTROL pin asserts exactly one `fr_ledger` insert, that its id is the row in the table, and no `fr_watch` entry.
- **A record-change flow fires through the production trigger path: right.** The triggering record is written through `hooks.run` as the signed-in dev admin. That is an ObjectQL write, so the record-change trigger the boot bound fires the flow as a save does. A create or write leg inserts the record. An update leg seeds it through `seed` (which sets `skipTriggers`, so the seed fires nothing) and then saves it unchanged. A delete leg seeds it and then deletes it. An array-form `triggerType` falls back to an insert, which fires its create leg. The CONTROL pin proves the real path: `verdict` is `completed` and the ledger row exists.
- **Only read seams of service-automation: right.** `FlowRunAutomation` is `Pick` of `getFlow`, `listRuns`, `getFlowRuntimeStates` and `getUnknownNodeTypeAudit`. The start goes through the verify handle's existing doors (`hooks.run`, `flows.run`). Nothing under `packages/services/service-automation` changes.
- **Write confinement, refused before the other driver is called: right.** `confineToEphemeral` registers one global ObjectQL middleware for each engine. For `insert`, `update`, `delete`, `purge` and `restore` on an object whose `getDriverForObject` is not the default driver instance, it throws `PERMISSION_DENIED` with status 403 before `next()`. The middleware chain runs ahead of the executor, and each of those five verbs is dispatched through `executeWithMiddleware` at `origin/main`. So the other driver is never reached. The registration comes before the seed and the start, so the seed of an update or delete leg is confined too. With no default driver, the run is not started (`confinement_unavailable`). The pin uses a recording driver on an external, writable datasource. It asserts the refusal, the node, the datasource named, exactly one confined entry in `writes` and an unchanged call log. The dev's ablation of the one guarding line turned it red, and the remote driver received the insert.
- **The new `@objectstack/verify` exports, and what the built cli reaches: right.** `index.ts` adds `runFlowProof` and `formatFlowRunReport`, and nine types. The runtime imports of `flow-run.ts` are `@objectstack/core` (`isServiceNotRegisteredError`, on its root entry) and `@objectstack/spec/automation` (`collectFlowGraphs`, through `export *` of `control-flow.zod`). Both are already runtime dependencies of the package. The `objectql` and `service-automation` imports are type-only. The cli reaches the two functions through its existing `@objectstack/verify` import. `Build Core`, including the require-entry load step, succeeded.
- **Anything removed, renamed or narrowed: nothing.** No existing export, flag, JSON member or exit condition changes. The `flowRun` member is present only with `--flow`. The `NOT_A_STAND_IN` entries add two names to a gate list and remove none.
- **SQL push-down: no finding.** The diff adds no data query. The run-log diff is a set difference over at most 100 ids per call on the engine's own history, on a fresh stack, and it is not a join over records.

Findings:

- **S1 (should-fix): a flow that the deployment's scheduled-work policy keeps unarmed is reported as a defect and fails `os verify`.** `FLOW_UNBOUND_CAUSES` at `origin/main` (`packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts`) says that `deployment_policy` is an operator setting and "Not a defect", and the engine's `describeUnboundReason` must never call it a binding failure. `runFlowProof` treats every `bound: false` the same way. It reports kind `trigger_unbound` with "the flow's trigger ... never binds, so nothing ever starts it", and that counts as a hard failure. The PR's own smoke shows the effect: `todo_task_reminder` in `examples/app-todo` gives `trigger_unbound` because the policy is off by default. So in a default environment, every schedule or time-relative flow fails `os verify --flow`, including the `--flow nightly_cleanup --json` form the PR adds to the command's examples, and the reader is told the flow is broken. To close it, branch on `report.trigger.cause`. For `deployment_policy`, either start the run through the no-caller path anyway (the graph is still what is under test) with a note naming the switch, or report `not_run` with that note and leave it out of the hard-failure count. Add one pin for that cause. The original reviewer reads the delta.
- **S2 (should-fix): the no-caller start does not give the flow the record that its trigger would give it.** The docs and the changeset say a schedule or API-triggered flow "is started the way that trigger starts it". The code sends every flow whose trigger is not record-change through `flows.run(..., { system: true })`, which passes `--flow-input` as `params` only. At `origin/main`, the API trigger passes the request body as both `record` and `params` (`trigger-api/src/api-trigger.ts`), and a `time_relative` sweep passes each swept row as `record` (`trigger-schedule/src/time-relative-trigger.ts`; `flow-cel-root-scope.ts` lists both as entry points that pass a record). Here those flows run with no `record`, so a node that reads `record.*` fails or takes the wrong branch, even though the flow works in production. That gives a false `node_failed` and a non-zero exit. `--flow-record` is ignored for these flows ("only a record-change flow starts from a record"). To close it, either pass the record these two triggers pass (`--flow-input` as `record` and `params` for `api`, and `--flow-record` as `record` for `time_relative`), or narrow the sentence in the docs, the changeset and the flag help to what the code does. Either fix needs a pin.
- **S3 (should-fix, escalated to the seat): outbound nodes run for real, and the flag help does not say so.** Every data write is confined (①). Nodes of type `http`, `connector_action`, `notify` and `script` that call out are not, and `os verify` loads the project's `.env*` files first, so they run with whatever credentials the project holds. The card's scope line reads "A flow that would write runs against the ephemeral stack only". A `connector_action` that creates a record in an external system is a write outside the stack under a plain reading. The PR states the boundary clearly in `cli.mdx` and the changeset, and area note 6987264675 hands the judgment here. I judge that it does not fully meet the card's line, but that it is not a must-fix: the card's Done-when is met, the confinement covers every write path a data node has, and the gap is disclosed. Two parts. (a) The `--flow` flag description, which is the text `os verify --help` shows, says only "Every write outside the in-memory database this run boots is refused before its datasource is called". It does not have the docs' "a node that calls out runs for real". Add that sentence. (b) The seat takes a ruling on whether the card's "write" covers outbound calls. If it does, a guard is cheap in this diff: refuse to start a flow whose definition holds one of those node types unless an explicit opt-in flag is given, and name the nodes in the report.
- **N1 (nit): the reported writes depend on the order the middleware was registered.** `writes` adds the confinement's refusals after the observer's entries. That gives one entry per refused write only because the confinement middleware is registered before `observeWrites` installs the observer, which makes it the outer middleware, so the observer never sees the refused write. That holds for the cli's fresh stack and for the test suite. A caller of the exported `runFlowProof` on a stack that has already used `observeWrites` gets each refused write listed twice. Dropping observed writes whose error is the confinement's would make this independent of order. The cli path is not affected.
- **N2 (nit): the update leg, the delete leg and the no-caller start have no pin.** The four pins cover an insert leg, the missing executor, the unbound trigger and the confinement. The seed-then-save and seed-then-delete legs, the `system` start, and the skipped and paused verdicts are read but not pinned. The code is right where it is read, apart from S1 and S2.

### ② Semver level

- **Changeset `.changeset/34779-verify-flow-run.md`: right.** It bumps `@objectstack/verify` and `@objectstack/cli` at `patch`. Those are exactly the two published packages whose source changes. The gate script, the docs page and the tests are not published. AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist item 3 says `Metadata-protocol: none` takes `patch`, and a widening outside the protocol ships `patch`. CI `Check Changeset` succeeded on this head.
- **`Clause-②: yes (widening)`: right.** It starts its line in the PR body (`yes (widening)`) and in the changeset (`yes (widening: a new ...)`). The annotated form of the arm has precedent on `main`, and the checks that read it are green. A new option and new exports, with nothing removed, renamed or newly refused, are a widening. Claim 6983783896 declared `Clause-②: yes`.
- **`Metadata-protocol: none`: right.** No spec key, accepted value or metadata type is added. The flow, trigger and node vocabulary is read as it already stands.
- **Changeset and `cli.mdx` prose against the diff: right, except for S1, S2 and S3(a).**
  - "each node's status as the run's log records it, the first failure with its code and the node named, and every write the run made": true (①).
  - "A record-change flow is fired by its own trigger ... inserted for a create or write leg; seeded and saved unchanged for an update leg; seeded and deleted for a delete leg": true.
  - "A schedule, an API-triggered flow or a flow declared `runAs: 'system'` is started with no caller, as its trigger starts it": the no-caller part is true. "As its trigger starts it" is not true for `api` and `time_relative` (S2).
  - "A node whose type no installed plugin runs is named, whether the run reached it or not. A flow whose trigger never binds is reported with the trigger and the engine's reason, and is not run": true. It also catches a flow that is only switched off by policy (S1).
  - "a write to an object bound to any other datasource is refused before that datasource's driver is called, and the node that made it fails naming the object and the datasource. Nodes that call out ... run for real": true (①, S3).
  - The failure list and the not-counted list (skipped, paused): true as coded, with S1's policy case on the failure side.
  - "`--json` carries the report as `flowRun`", and the JSON section's member list: true.
  - New exports listed: true, and complete.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Open questions: none in the report.
- Deviation, the two `NOT_A_STAND_IN` entries in `scripts/check-verify-stand-in-erasure.mjs`: answered and right. The gate requires every new export to be classified, both functions take the same `VerifyStack` handle as the families already listed, and the edit only adds to the list. Accepted in 6987264675.
- Deviation, the sibling `flow-json-flag.ts` helper: answered and right. It keeps the test from importing the command module. The seven cases cover absent, object, unparseable, array, string, null and number.
- Deviation, `test:repo` and the cli integration tier left to CI: answered. No integration-tier file or spawn entry is touched. CI `Test Core` carries them, and 6 of its shards are still running (①).
- NOT-MEASURED `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`: answered. The `Build Core` step that runs it succeeded on this head.
- Deviation, the PR body footer form: process only.
- Port provenance from cloud `c21b372`: accepted in 6987264675. Only behaviour moved, and the diff holds no key, endpoint or tenant material.
- The boundary for outbound nodes, judged against the card's "a flow that would write runs against the ephemeral stack only" and the docs that state it: S3. Escalated to the seat for the ruling in S3(b). S3(a) is a one-sentence help-text change.
- Out-of-scope note, the existing CRUD phase may admit writable objects on a declared external datasource: this diff does not change it. The flow run boots its own stack, and its confinement does not reach the CRUD phase that runs earlier in the same `os verify --flow` command. It is the seat's to decide, as area note 6987264675 says. It is not judged here.
- `security_findings: none`: I agree for this diff.
- Ablations: four mutations, one for each pin, each turned red and was restored to the HEAD blob. The first CONTROL and confinement attempts were no-ops that the tool refused, and the re-runs with markers landed. No ablation covers the policy cause (S1), the no-caller record (S2) or the update and delete legs (N2).
- Process notes: the PR is a draft. Author: `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (relay), assignee `os-warren`, so no extra author note is owed. S1 and S2 need a new head, and the original reviewer reads the delta. S3(a) can ride on that head, and S3(b) waits on the seat's ruling. Before landing, the seat must also see the 6 running `Test Core` shards finish green on the final head (①).

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `f1b566279d8b071c0363ed2b4cb2a6a90c624fd5`
Local-runs: none

Round 2. It reads the delta from `348cc18de6` (record 6987485237) to this head.

Inputs: the seat's S3 ruling A, as the coordinator relayed it (outbound nodes are not executed under `os verify --flow`; the run stops at the first one with a named `outbound_not_run` result; no opt-in flag); os-dev round-2 report 6989017033 on #34779; the PR body as the seat rewrote it at 19:21Z; and `git diff 348cc18de6 f1b566279d`. The diff holds four PR commits (`ffa765fe85`, `97bd03bdec`, `07a5495f11`, `f1b566279d`) and the merge of origin/main `f2078e3674` (`22bb6ff090`). I judged only the four PR commits. The merge changes none of this PR's files: between `348cc18de6` and `22bb6ff090` the diff of those files is empty. I also read the check-runs on this head. Code outside the diff was read at `origin/main` only.

Face: unchanged. The PR's file list against its new merge-base `f2078e3674` is the same nine files as in round 1, with no `packages/spec/src/**` path and no governed path. `Governed Surface Queue Guard` succeeded on this head. This is still the declaration face at `TIER_DEFAULT`, with no ④.

### ① Derived judgments
